**Operator ruling (Rico, 2026-08-06), recorded:** "we don't really want to be putting caps on things. We just want to make sure that stupid shit like that giant file doesn't go through the system... Can we just fix that one thing and break it down into its component pieces properly and move the fuck on from ever thinking about an almost 50 MB chunk trying to go through?"

**Measured facts (this session, live dogfood DB open_brain_local_20260724):**
- The 4 largest thoughts (~857 KB each) are raw Claude Code session-transcript JSONL dumps, source `planning-skippy-agentspace`, ingested 2026-03-17 and re-ingested 2026-06-19 (2 distinct contents x 2 copies). No images exist anywhere in the corpus.
- Distribution: 24,664 of 25,192 thoughts are under 10 KB; 524 are 10-100 KB; only these 4 above.
- The 47.6 MB worst-case trace was these rows x 750-candidate fetch x 5 redundant copies. Dedup (merged in #599's fix delta, operator-approved) removes the x5.
- Chunking machinery EXISTS (`src/chunking.ts` CHUNK_THRESHOLD=2000, `src/chunk-write.ts`) — but `parent_id` is NULL on every row in the table and 53 KB rows landed as recently as July, so the primary write path is not chunking. UNVERIFIED which paths use chunk-write vs bypass it — the lane verifies.

**Work:**
1. **Data remediation (operator-authorized):** decompose the 4 transcript rows into proper component pieces through the existing chunking/decomposition machinery; originals go through the normal lifecycle (`discarded_entries`/archive with provenance pointing at the replacements) — nothing hard-deleted. Receipts: before/after row counts, sizes, and a search that used to surface a monster row now surfacing its pieces.
2. **Code (PR):** remove the 300-char slice in the evidence projections (both trees) — full content flows into retrieval evidence again. KEEP the dedup (ids/counts in rank input) and KEEP the 256 KiB degradation strictly as an emergency backstop against pathological payloads (it should never fire on the post-remediation corpus — add a note saying exactly that at the constant).
3. **Investigation (report on this issue, fix only if small and owned):** why do multi-KB writes bypass the chunker — which write paths call chunk-write and which don't, and what the intended design is (docs/decisions/, dream-design). If the fix is bigger than a bounded change, file it as its own issue.

Per the standing order-of-operations rule: this removes a cap on real data and fixes the root; the only remaining bound is the backstop against exactly the garbage class the operator named.
